description: The complete model_type vocabulary the tracebloc platform accepts, across ALL task types. metaApi.models.Experiment.model_type is a Django CharField with choices=MODEL_TYPE_CHOICES, so a value outside this set is refused by the ChoiceField at experiment creation with a 400 -- before the model file is looked at, and with nothing in the error naming the template as the cause. Published here so the model-zoo can assert in its own CI that every template's declared model_type is one the platform can actually store (model-zoo#273). This is a SUPERSET of the per-task-type routing vocabularies: object_detection_families.v2.json narrows the OD subset to {rcnn, torchvision_detection, yolo}, and the engine's keypoint strategy routes only {rcnn, heatmap} specially. Membership here means STORABLE, not necessarily well-routed for a given category.

generated_from.method: ast.parse of Experiment.MODEL_TYPE_CHOICES, resolving each choice's MODEL_TYPE_* constant to its string literal. Derived mechanically, never hand-transcribed -- a hand-copied list is how the OD vocabulary drift shipped.

blank_note: The field is blank=True/null=True and ExperimentSerializer.validate_model_type coerces a falsy value to 'default', so an empty declaration is STORED, not refused. Most zoo templates declare "". Note this is only about the backend: the engine's keypoint _infer_model_type falls an empty value through to an RCNN_FAMILY fallback, so "" is not automatically the right declaration for a keypoint model.

not_accepted.description: Values a producer has actually shipped that this ChoiceField refuses. Listed explicitly so a consumer's check reports them by name rather than as an anonymous miss.

notes.transformer: Declared by three keypoint templates (sapiens, vitpose, vitpose_plus) until model-zoo#273. Never a member of MODEL_TYPE_CHOICES; an experiment built from any of the three was refused with a 400.
notes.hf_transformer: WAS a choice and is not one now -- (internal ref) retired the DETR/HuggingFace detection family and removed it from MODEL_TYPE_CHOICES. Kept here so a template reintroducing it fails by name.

matching: Django's ChoiceField compares the stored string exactly. The engine's resolvers lowercase and strip before their own lookups, so a consumer check that normalises the same way is no weaker on values already lowercase -- every value above is.
